label: Late original positions and <DEL> in long sequences, gated by which token opened the sequence
explanation: Fires only on the input side: late original positions (orig_idx 4-8, rate rising to ~40% at orig_idx 8) and the <DEL> step (20% rate, 30% of mass). It never fires in the copy phase or at t<=3. The timing condition (phase<=1 & t>=5) alone covers 97% of activations and 98% of mass, but precision is only 0.25, so it is far from sufficient. Whether it fires depends strongly on the early contents of the sequence, mostly the first token: first_tok in s/w/v/c gives ~2.6x lift, and j/e/t/f/u/n give smaller lift. Adding the first-token set gives dev F1 0.55, and a second token in s/w/v/c adds a little more recall. This looks like a distributed readout of the start of the sequence carried in the hidden state, not a crisp rule. Magnitude grows with position, is highest around t=6-8 and at <DEL>, and is larger when in_tok is the first occurrence of that token. The top examples often have h at the last original position.
